rounds.question: 100 kg?

explain.title: WHY IT WORKS
lines: Each egg is a tiny arch

source: Sutanto et al., Communications Physics (2025), MIT
Simulated: 46 N per egg, load shared evenly
caption: Can 24 eggs hold a grown adult? 🥚 One egg: 4.7 kg. Twelve: 56 kg. Twenty-four: 113 kg. Would you stand on them? What should we test next? 👇 #egg #physics #science #engineering #satisfying #mythbusting #3d
description: How much weight can eggs carry? We press one egg, then a carton of 12, then a carton of 24, all standing upright, and ask whether they could hold an 80 kg person.
One egg standing on its tip cracks at 46 N on average in MIT's lab tests, about 4.7 kg. The curved shell works like an arch: it turns the load into compression spread all around the shell.
Twelve eggs sharing the load can take about 12 x 4.7 = 56 kg: not enough for an 80 kg person. Twenty-four eggs take about 24 x 4.7 = 113 kg: enough to hold that person.
The catch: this only works if every egg carries the same share. If one egg sits higher, or a heel presses on one spot, that egg takes much more than its share and cracks first.
The animation is a simulation using the average crack load from the study below, multiplied by the number of eggs.
sources_detail: Sutanto, Cohen et al., 'Challenging common notions on how eggs break and the role of strength versus toughness', Communications Physics 8, 182 (2025), MIT. doi:10.1038/s42005-025-02087-0
Static compression to first crack, egg standing (vertical): 46.0 +/- 6.6 N -> 46.0 / 9.81 = 4.69 kg
12 eggs: 12 x 46.0 N = 552 N = 56.3 kg ; 24 eggs: 24 x 46.0 N = 1104 N = 112.5 kg (shown as 113 kg). Assumes the load is shared equally.
